questions.prompt: What does DSP stand for, and what does it do?
questions.answer: Demand-Side Platform: software advertisers use to buy digital ad opportunities automatically, often through auctions. It can evaluate the opportunity, audience, creative and bid against the advertiser's goal and budget.
checklist: Explains it is on the advertiser/buyer side
Mentions automated ad buying or bidding
questions.misconception: A DSP is not the publisher's selling platform; that is generally an SSP.

questions.prompt: What is real-time bidding (RTB)?
questions.answer: An automated auction for an individual digital ad impression. The auction usually happens in a fraction of a second when a publisher makes ad space available.

questions.prompt: Which platform mainly helps advertisers buy ad inventory?
questions.answer: A DSP is on the advertiser/demand side. An SSP helps a publisher sell its available inventory.

questions.prompt: Explain retargeting in one sentence and give a simple example.
questions.answer: Retargeting shows relevant ads to people who already interacted with a business. For example, someone views trainers in a shop and later sees an ad for those trainers.
questions.misconception: A retargeted person can still be a first-time buyer; prior interaction does not mean prior purchase.

questions.prompt: What is a branding campaign, and how might success be measured?
questions.answer: A campaign aimed at awareness, recognition, preference or engagement. Depending on the goal, useful measures could include relevant reach, viewability, video completion or brand lift.
checklist: Does not assume only immediate purchases matter

questions.prompt: Choose a useful simplified purchase funnel.
questions.answer: Awareness → consideration → purchase → retention is a useful simplified model. Real customer journeys can skip, repeat or cross stages.

questions.prompt: Why might an ad platform report more clicks than GA4 reports sessions?
questions.answer: Clicks and sessions are different metrics. Multiple clicks may fall within one session; someone may leave before analytics loads; tracking, redirects, consent, tagging, attribution scope, processing or filtering may differ. First align definitions, dates and campaign scope, then investigate the journey.
checklist: Gives at least two plausible causes
Avoids assuming fraud or blaming one system

questions.prompt: In a simple GTM explanation, what is the difference between tag, trigger and variable?
options: What runs; when it runs; the value/data it uses
When it runs; what runs; the destination
All three mean the same thing
questions.answer: A tag performs an action, a trigger determines when it runs, and a variable provides a value used by the configuration.

questions.prompt: What is the dataLayer, and why does a dataLayer push not by itself prove an event was tracked?
questions.answer: It is a structured JavaScript data object used to make event details available to tag configurations. A push alone does not show that a trigger matched, a tag fired, the request was sent, or the receiving system processed it.
checklist: A push only enters data into the layer

questions.prompt: In Chrome, where can you inspect a site's cookies?
questions.answer: Open DevTools → Application → Storage → Cookies, then select the relevant origin. Use Network as well if checking whether a cookie was sent with a request. HttpOnly cookies are not accessible through document.cookie.

questions.prompt: What would you check on an ecommerce purchase event?
questions.answer: It should represent a confirmed purchase. Check event timing, unique transaction ID, numeric value, currency, item/product IDs, duplicate firing, failed payments, page reload behaviour and whether it reaches the expected destination.
checklist: Confirmed outcome rather than button click

questions.prompt: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
options: == permits type coercion; === compares without type coercion
questions.answer: == may convert values before comparison; === compares without type coercion. Strict equality is a clear default.

questions.prompt: What is the value and type of `var a = 3 + 2 + "7"`?
questions.answer: Addition runs left to right: 3 + 2 is numeric 5; then 5 + "7" joins into the string "57".

questions.prompt: Why might adding a price from an HTML field produce an unexpected result?
questions.answer: Values read from fields are often strings. With `+`, JavaScript may concatenate text, such as `"20" + 5` producing `"205"`. Convert and validate numeric data before arithmetic.

questions.prompt: What is CTR? Calculate it for 1,000 clicks and 100,000 impressions.
questions.answer: CTR = clicks ÷ impressions × 100. Here it is 1%.

questions.prompt: A campaign spends £600 and gets 30 purchases. What is CPA?
questions.answer: CPA = spend ÷ defined conversions = £600 ÷ 30 = £20 per purchase.

questions.prompt: Spend is £500 and attributed revenue is £3,200. What is ROAS, and does that prove profit?
questions.answer: ROAS = attributed revenue ÷ ad spend = 6.4x (640%). It does not by itself prove profit; margin, returns, discounts and other costs matter.

questions.prompt: Conversion rate moves from 2% to 3%. What is the percentage-point change and the relative increase?
questions.answer: +1 percentage point. Relative increase is (3-2) ÷ 2 = 50%.

questions.prompt: A client asks whether CPC or CPS is better. What is your first question?
questions.answer: Ask what CPS means (cost per sale or cost per session) and what outcome the client wants. Then compare expected unit cost, quality, volume, measurement and attribution under the same assumptions.
checklist: Compare on consistent definitions and evidence
questions.misconception: A billing model is not automatically a better result or safer campaign.

questions.prompt: Why is attributed ROAS alone not proof that a retargeting campaign generated incremental sales?
questions.answer: Retargeting reaches people already likely to buy. Attribution allocates credit under chosen rules; it does not show what would have happened without the ad. A well-designed holdout/experiment can estimate incremental impact.

questions.prompt: Give a simple sequence for investigating a tracking or integration problem.
questions.answer: Reproduce it; define expected versus actual; inspect the event/request and data; compare a working journey; isolate the cause; fix or escalate with evidence; retest; update the client.

questions.prompt: Practice case: an ad platform shows 10,000 clicks while GA4 shows 6,500 campaign sessions. What do you tell the client and check first?
questions.answer: Do not assume 3,500 people were lost. First align metric, date, timezone, campaign scope and attribution. Clicks and sessions differ. Then segment where the gap began and test landing-page load, redirects/parameters, tag firing, consent, blockers, and reporting delay. Report confirmed causes and remaining uncertainty.
questions.label: Fictional interview practice data

questions.prompt: A purchase event fires twice for some orders after a site change. What do you investigate?
questions.answer: Reproduce one test order, compare timestamps and transaction IDs, inspect request initiators and recent changes, and determine whether there are duplicate tags/containers, event handlers or reloads. Compare against completed backend orders if authorised. Fix the identified cause and retest successful, failed and reload paths.
checklist: Separate tracking duplication from actual orders

questions.prompt: What does programmatic advertising mean?
questions.answer: Using software and automated processes to buy, sell or deliver digital advertising. Real-time bidding is one programmatic method; programmatic buying is the broader idea.
checklist: RTB is one method, not a synonym for all programmatic

questions.prompt: What do a publisher, SSP and ad exchange do in a programmatic auction?
questions.answer: A publisher provides the content and ad space. An SSP helps the publisher offer that inventory to buyers. An ad exchange connects buying and selling systems and facilitates auctions. The exact setup can vary.

questions.prompt: What is a conversion in a campaign?
questions.answer: A user action defined as valuable for a campaign, such as a purchase, lead or app install. Confirm the exact event and rules with the client before analysing results.

questions.prompt: What is CPM? Spend is £240 for 80,000 impressions. Calculate the CPM.
questions.answer: CPM is cost per thousand impressions: spend ÷ impressions × 1,000. £240 ÷ 80,000 × 1,000 = £3 CPM.

questions.prompt: What is CPC? Spend is £180 for 600 clicks.
questions.answer: CPC is spend divided by clicks: £180 ÷ 600 = £0.30 per click.

questions.prompt: A landing page gets 800 sessions and 40 purchases. What is the purchase conversion rate, using sessions as the denominator?
questions.answer: Purchases ÷ sessions × 100 = 40 ÷ 800 × 100 = 5%. State the denominator because conversion rate can be calculated from clicks, sessions or users depending on the agreed definition.

questions.prompt: Revenue is £4,800 from 60 orders. What is average order value (AOV)?
questions.answer: AOV is revenue divided by orders: £4,800 ÷ 60 = £80 per order. Check whether revenue includes tax, shipping, discounts or refunds in the reporting definition.

questions.prompt: What does average ad frequency mean, and what might unusually high frequency suggest?
questions.answer: Average frequency is impressions divided by reached people over a defined period. High frequency may mean the same audience is seeing ads repeatedly; check reach, campaign goal, time window and performance before recommending a frequency cap or audience change.
checklist: Treats high frequency as a signal to investigate, not automatic proof of fatigue

questions.prompt: What is a marketing tag or conversion pixel used for?
questions.answer: It is code or a configured measurement call that sends defined event information to an analytics or advertising system. A tag firing in the browser does not by itself prove the receiving platform accepted, attributed or reported it.
checklist: Can be code or a managed tag
Firing is not the same as successful reporting

questions.prompt: What is an MMP, and what does it help an app marketer measure?
questions.answer: A Mobile Measurement Partner helps measure app campaign performance and attribution across advertising channels, including app installs and in-app events. It is not the same thing as a website tag manager.

questions.prompt: What is a product feed, and what would you check if a dynamic ad shows the wrong item?
questions.answer: A product feed is a structured catalogue of items and attributes such as product ID, name, price, availability and image. Compare the ID sent in the product-view event with the feed ID, then check field mapping, freshness, variants, currency and image URLs.
checklist: Match event item ID to feed item ID

questions.prompt: In JavaScript, what type of value is returned by `typeof "7"`?
questions.answer: The quotes make `"7"` a string. `typeof "7"` returns `"string"`; `typeof 7` returns `"number"`.

questions.prompt: What is the practical difference between a JavaScript array and an object?
questions.answer: An array is commonly used for an ordered list of values, accessed by numeric index such as `items[0]`. An object groups named properties, accessed with dot or bracket notation such as `product.id` or `product["id"]`.
checklist: Can read a simple access expression

questions.prompt: Read this: `button.addEventListener("click", sendEvent)`. What does it mean?
questions.answer: When the button receives a click event, the browser calls the `sendEvent` function. `sendEvent` is passed as a callback here; it is not called immediately because there are no parentheses after its name.
checklist: Distinguishes function reference from immediate call

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between `const` and `let` for a variable declaration?
options: `const` cannot be reassigned; `let` can be reassigned
questions.answer: A `const` binding cannot be reassigned, while a `let` binding can. A `const` object may still have its properties changed; `const` does not make it deeply immutable.

questions.prompt: What does customer experience (CX) mean in a technical account role?
questions.answer: CX is the customer’s overall experience across interactions with a company. In a technical account role, clear updates, reliable implementation, quick evidence-based troubleshooting and setting realistic expectations all contribute to it.
checklist: Avoids reducing CX to friendliness alone

questions.prompt: The client confirms orders in its ecommerce system, but the ad platform reports no purchases. Walk through your first checks.
questions.answer: Confirm the event definition and time range, then place an authorised test order if possible. Check whether the purchase event and required values/IDs are generated, whether the tag fires, whether the network request succeeds, whether the platform receives the event, and whether attribution/reporting delay or consent affects visibility. Record evidence at each step and escalate with a reproducible example.
checklist: Check consent, identifiers, delay and deduplication
Give client findings and next action

questions.prompt: A client says the retargeting ad shows a product different from the one a shopper viewed. What do you compare?
questions.answer: Compare the product ID in the view event with the ID in the catalogue/feed and the item selected in the creative. Then inspect variant mapping, case/format differences, feed refresh time and whether the event is sent at the correct page state. Reproduce with one known product ID.
checklist: Trace one known product end to end
Check variants, formatting and feed freshness

questions.prompt: A client says ROAS fell sharply this week. What do you check before changing campaign settings?
questions.answer: Verify the metric, date range, attribution window and data completeness first. Compare spend, clicks, conversions, revenue, average order value, product mix, tracking changes, stock/pricing and site checkout health against a comparable period. Segment the change, then agree a measured action and monitoring window with the account team.
